items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: I had a boy fellow from Philadelphia came in there named Charley Gaines, see, and he worked with me until, in fact until I finished that job.

ctx.x: It wasn't called much of nothing. But I don't know what we named it. Anyhow, it was in St. Catherine Street, right down the street from the Royal Garden. Everybody who's been to Detroit know where St. Catherine Street -- right off of -- I don't even remember the street, now. A big street. I don't know. Anyhow, so when we took this cabaret we had seven entertainers and there was five of us in the band. And of course, Charley Dixon and Elmer Albert Chambers and I took the cabaret because the other two boys said,…

But at the same time, we were losing money. Because I found out one thing, you can't play and watch the cash register, too. So we couldn't do that, we found that we couldn't do that. So we played good music. Jimmy was a good piano player, I mean a good trombone player. And Elmer Chambers, incidentally, was in the war with me. And Charley Dixon played very well. Later on he was an arranger with Chick Webb. And Elmer Chambers worked with Fletcher Henderson after he left me, see. Because I had a boy fellow from…
